evolutionary_track_source.metallicity_note: Z=0.019 (Y=0.273) is the paper's own identified solar-composition value (Sect. 2: "almost identical to the Z=0.01886 favoured by Anders & Grevesse 1989"), appropriate for this Sun-like system.
evolutionary_track_source.status_note: [2026-08-29] Real Girardi (2000) evolutionary-track/isochrone data was obtained and run against this system: VizieR catalog J/A+AS/141/371 (tables mstracks, isochron), Z=0.019 (Y=0.273), Overshoot=1. Source data: Girardi et al. (2000), A&AS, 141, 371, doi:10.1051/aas:2000126. Loader: pyseshat.evolution.parsers.girardi2000.load_girardi2000_vizier_tracks/_isochrones, wired as this project's default grid via pyseshat.evolution.grids.load_default_evolution_model(). Pipeline: pyseshat.evolution.benchmark_checks.run_system_evolutionary_check (nearest_track -> fit_track independently per component -> fit_common_age jointly), the same code scripts/run_evolutionary_checks.py and scripts/generate_benchmark_plots.py's generate_hrdiagrams() both use, so this recorded result, the numeric report, and the HR-diagram figure cannot silently drift apart. mass_source: derived from literature SB2 orbital elements (Torres et al. 2015 Table 1, P/e/i/K1/K2) via analysis.masses.component_masses_from_elements -- no separately-stated literature mass exists in this repository. M1=2.5688, M2=2.4828 Msun. primary: requested M=2.569 Msun -> nearest track M=2.5 Msun (2.68% off); independent best-fit age=7.676e+08 yr (0.77 Gyr), chi2=0.481, state=giant (log g < 3.0). secondary: requested M=2.483 Msun -> nearest track M=2.5 Msun (0.69% off); independent best-fit age=5.920e+08 yr (0.59 Gyr), chi2=4.106, state=subgiant (3.0 <= log g < 4.0). independent-fit age_difference: 1.756e+08 yr (0.18 Gyr) (22.9% of the older independent age). common-age (joint) fit: age=5.923e+08 yr (0.59 Gyr), chi2=45.229, primary log g=3.035 (subgiant (3.0 <= log g < 4.0)), secondary log g=3.035 (subgiant (3.0 <= log g < 4.0)). No prior age/mass/evolutionary-stage numbers for this system existed anywhere else in this project's documentation before this run -- there is nothing to compare against for a discrepancy; this is the first time such numbers have been computed here. (Separate comparison against the source paper's own stated age, if any, was not performed as part of this run.)

evolutionary_track_source.prior_grid: None -- no evolutionary-track grid (Girardi, PARSEC, or otherwise) had ever been run against this system before this entry; PARSEC parsing infrastructure existed in the codebase but with zero bundled data and zero benchmark wiring.

data_provenance: SYNTHETIC measurements: combined-light magnitudes are generated from this file's own literature Teff/R/logg via PySeshat's own synthetic_binary_magnitudes(), plus Gaussian noise at an ASSUMED 0.03 mag representative precision -- a forward-model self-consistency check (does fit_photometry recover known input Teff/R/E(B-V) from data generated by PySeshat's own model), not a comparison to independently-observed sky photometry. See scripts/build_joint_benchmarks.py module docstring.

metallicity.source: nearest available CK04 grid point (ckp00, [M/H]=0.0); literature [Fe/H]=-0.04 (Torres et al. 2015) is not itself used. Re-verified 2026-09-02 after the full 608-file CK04 grid (all 8 metallicity slices) was downloaded: this system's photometric measurements are SYNTHETIC, forward-modeled by this same pipeline's synthetic_binary_magnitudes() at metallicity=0.0 (scripts/build_joint_benchmarks.py) -- so fitting at 0.0 is the self-consistent choice for this benchmark's actual purpose (validating the fitting pipeline recovers the parameters used to generate its own synthetic input), not merely a data-availability fallback. Fitting at a metallicity closer to the true literature value (e.g. -0.04 is itself closer to 0.0 than to any other grid step, so this is moot for Capella specifically) would introduce a deliberate synthetic-data/fit-grid mismatch rather than remove one.

radius_prior_note: 10% relative sigma Gaussian prior on each component's radius, tied to the literature value -- same convention as the other four Al-Wardat systems.
